input.candidate_statement: I build a lowercase alphanumeric copy, reverse it, and compare.

problem_context.title: Valid Palindrome
problem_context.statement: Given a string s, return true if its alphanumeric characters read the same forward and backward after ignoring case. Ignore all non-alphanumeric characters.

items: s contains ASCII letters, digits, punctuation, and spaces.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

examples.explanation: The normalized characters do not mirror each other.

arguments.s: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

expected_approaches.summary: Move pointers inward, skipping non-alphanumeric characters and comparing lowercase forms.
expected_approaches.applicability: A string can be scanned from both ends and normalization is local.
assumptions: The selected alphanumeric and case-normalization operations match the stated input domain.
key_invariants: All normalized characters outside the active pointer interval have already matched their mirror.
tradeoffs: Avoids an allocated filtered copy but requires careful pointer movement.
common_failure_modes: advancing only one pointer after a match

alternative_approaches.summary: Build a lowercase alphanumeric string, then compare it with its reverse or scan it from both ends.
alternative_approaches.applicability: When clarity matters more than constant auxiliary space.
key_invariants: The filtered copy preserves exactly the relevant normalized character sequence.
tradeoffs: Simpler normalization but allocates another string.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: bool isPalindrome(string s){ int left=0,right=(int)s.size()-1; while(left<right){ while(left<right && !isalnum((unsigned char)s[left])) left++; while(left<right && !isalnum((unsigned char)s[right])) right--; if(tolower((unsigned char)s[left])!=tolower((unsigned char)s[right])) return false; left++; right--; } return true; } };

class Solution { public boolean isPalindrome(String s){ int left=0,right=s.length()-1; while(left<right){ while(left<right&&!Character.isLetterOrDigit(s.charAt(left))) left++; while(left<right&&!Character.isLetterOrDigit(s.charAt(right))) right--; if(Character.toLowerCase(s.charAt(left))!=Character.toLowerCase(s.charAt(right))) return false; left++; right--; } return true; } }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: All already-passed relevant character pairs match after normalization.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Explain why each input position is considered at most once and no copy is required.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: Normalize before comparing rather than treating punctuation as meaningful.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Advance both pointers after equal normalized characters.
Skip irrelevant characters independently on either side.

edge_cases.diagnostic_goal: An empty relevant sequence is palindromic.

counterexamples.input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

counterexamples.purpose: Normalizes to an empty character sequence.
Exposes comparing the wrong normalized pair.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: Discuss how a broader text definition would require an explicit normalization policy.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend why discarded outer characters no longer need consideration.
Compare the filtered-copy approach with in-place pointers.

expected_good_signals: both pointers first land on relevant characters
sample_phrasings: When do you know each pointer is positioned on a character that matters?
What should this do for a string containing only punctuation and spaces?

common_followups.diagnostic_goal: Clarify the domain assumption behind character helpers.
expected_good_signals: ties implementation to specified character domain
weak_or_misconception_signals: claims any Unicode text is handled without a policy
sample_phrasings: What would you need to specify before extending this to arbitrary Unicode text?

level_considerations.guidance: Focus on the normalized comparison rule.
Expect a two-pointer invariant and O(1) auxiliary-space explanation.

interview_pack.reference_reasoning: The reviewed in-place scan is a strong baseline; filtered-copy and other correct normalizing approaches remain valid when their costs and semantics are clear.

technical_rationale_rubric.technical_issue: Explore an alternative's space tradeoff without implying the submitted approach is wrong.

review.description: A correct filtered-copy solution may be compared with an in-place scan.
review.manual_review_notes: Alternate correct approach is not a false positive.
